chapter_seo_title: Face to Face – Li Huowang Demands the Man Behind the Curtain
chapter_meta_description: Lyu Xiucai rushes to recruit help for his abducted master. But in the psychiatric ward, Li Huowang faces a brutal interrogation—and a threat against Yang Na that forces him to demand a face-to-face with the real power.
og_title: Face to Face – Li Huowang’s Cold Demand
og_description: Lyu Xiucai recruits allies while Li Huowang, under electroshock and a threat to Yang Na, demands to see the shadowy figure behind Wu Cheng.
twitter_title: Face to Face – Li Huowang Doesn’t Talk to Pawns
twitter_description: Lyu Xiucai hurries to save his master. Li Huowang, tortured by Wu Cheng, calmly asks for the person running the show.

lore_anchors.definition: In xianxia, a being who has achieved partial immortality or possesses a fragment of divine power—still above most mortal cultivators.
The ultimate goal of cultivation: shedding mortal limitations and rising to a higher plane of existence as a true immortal.
A Chinese idiom meaning that when someone rises to power, even their lowliest dependents benefit. Xiucai twists it to mock his family.
A pill that extends one’s lifespan. In this story, Wu Cheng’s organization covets Li Huowang’s ability to produce such a pill—or something far more dangerous.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Lyu Xiucai act so selfishly toward his family?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He believes his master holds the key to immortality, and he’s calculated that if he invests loyalty during the crisis, he’ll reap an ultimate technique reward—surpassing any family bond.
No. He reports to a “director” via video call and reveals that his organization has its own agenda separate from Yi Donglai’s. Li Huowang demands to see that person face to face.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Does the electroshock scene mean Li Huowang is defective?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. It shows his unbreakable will and his understanding that Wu Cheng can't kill him—only hurt him. It also reveals the lengths the organization will go to.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of Yang Na’s appearance?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She is Li Huowang’s childhood sweetheart and the modern-world anchor. By showing her surveillance footage, Wu Cheng demonstrates that he can reach the people Li Huowang cares about, forcing him to reconsider his defiance.
